course_info.trial_description:
1.  In the first ten minutes I will start off with a light conversation by introducing myself to the student and asking the student a few questions to 'break the ice'.  
2.  I willl then engage in an activity to assess the students level.  Questions in a minute:  Find a picture and ask questions about the picture and engage in a conversation.
3. In the second ten minutes I will start with a lesson.  I will explain that every lesson has a topic either chosen by myself or the student.   For eg. I could choose a Topic on Health.  We can together come up with a list of exercises - the student could list them in order of preference, from the most liked to the least liked.  We could then go onto to explain terms eg fitness, diet, health, exercises,   For more advanced students we can talk about mental, emotional health etc.  We could end off with a spelling Bee.
In the last 10 minutes I would thank the student for booking the class with me.  I would then go onto ask questions regarding motivation, ask a little more about themselves, what they want and expect from a lesson, is it a conversation or a more structured lesson.   I would then discuss what the future lessons would look like and go through the curriculum with them.  Ask them if they have concerns or suggestions.    End off with "Say what you see" - draw a picture on a white board that represents a phrase.  
Ask if they have any further questions or they could send me a message after the class.

pro_course_detail.title: Lesson
pro_course_detail.description:
1.  Start off with a little bit of a light easy conversation eg Introduce ourselves, ask where the student is from, etc.
2.  Get straight into an activity:  I will explain the plan before starting the activity and that is that we are going to test their level.
Activity:  Would you rather?  Eg. Be hot or cold; more time or more money; have a rewind button or a pause button; tam up with Wonder woman or Captain marvel; sing or dance; etc I will match the question to the level.  I would by now have assessed their skill level.

3. Start with the lesson:  Explain that every lesson will have a topic. They could choose it or I could choose it.  Tell them our topic for this lesson is on FOOD. Tell them what I am listening for eg. comparative words. This will give them a bit of a focus.
Go onto Google and find a picture with different types of food. Ask student to spot the differences or similarities between the pictures.
This gets them talking.  It gets them to engage using different comparative words and transition words as well.  
Thereafter I would ask them questions about the pictures.  Show them a link of different meals. Ask them to pick the ones that are the tastiest or saltiest or sweetest etc. or which has the most salt or most sugar.  Use different ways to get the student to include vocabulary for eg. which type of food is most popular in their country. etc
I will write them a few corrections so they know what their weaknesses are.
At the end get them to create a recipe. Give them steps and have them put them in order.
 
4.  In the last ten minutes I will thank them for booking a class with me.  I will go on to ask questions about what their goals are and given them an opportunity to tell me what they want and what to expect.  Ask them a little more about themselves.  
Discuss with the student what they can expect in the next lessons - go through it with them.  Ask if they have any concerns or suggestions or they could send me a message if they have any.
